instrument: esp_flash_get_size() via the bring-up sketch on COM7
note: Settles the 8 vs 16 MB conflict in favour of the board definition. The intuitive manual guess was wrong, and it was wrong in the direction that would have silently truncated an OTA partition.

instrument: Mitutoyo calipers on the bare PCB edge

note: The cell that actually arrived is narrower by 5 mm and thicker by 1 mm than the one originally planned, and both mattered - the back layout had to be re-solved.

instrument: Fluke 117, DC volts at the plug, before first connection
note: Metered BEFORE the first connection. SH1.25 polarity is not standardised and the housing gives you no clue.

instrument: printed alignment coupon against the panel, calipers
note: The active area is 3.05 mm off the module centre along the long axis. A symmetric 2.2 mm margin clips 0.85 mm off the active area, and the clipping is only visible once the shell is printed.

instrument: Mitutoyo calipers, receptacle centreline above the split plane
note: The assumed figure was measured from the wrong datum. The channel this drives is 0.64 mm short of the tallest legal USB-C plug boot, so measure your own cable.
38 x 23 mm is what pushed the body from 105 x 72 to 110 x 76 mm. One pin decision - no free ADC1 channel - moved the enclosure on two axes.

instrument: Mitutoyo calipers, over the fitted screw terminals
note: Measured over the terminals, not the bare board. Height conventions are where this kind of number usually goes wrong.

instrument: printed fit coupon, four bores tested
note: Bracketed: 20.6 is interior to the tested range, so the optimum is inside what was tried. Compare with the earlier 3.0/3.2/3.4/3.6 sweep where only 3.0 gripped - that one was bounded from the wrong end and the true optimum may be below 3.0.
Changed because CAD pushed back: the largest free disc anywhere in the back shell was 15.6 mm once the battery, speaker and expander had taken their space. The BOM moved, not the enclosure.

instrument: bring-up sketch timing a full refresh, Vext asserted and settled 100 ms first
note: Closed by watching a COUNTER INCREMENT, not by seeing a picture. E-ink retains its last image with no power, so a static demo image survives a dead driver, a wiped flash and an unpowered board. 1180 ms sits inside the 300-3000 ms plausibility band; an earlier 29 ms 'success' on a different board was the power-enable line being low.
